part5_watchtower.method: Recomputed the WATCHTOWER digest fresh from database/wt_ops_v2.db (read-only), reproducing the exact methodology used in docs/audits/storage_lifecycle_p5a_part21_watchtower_canonical_preservation.json and docs/audits/storage_lifecycle_p5b_r2_1_final_consumer_recensus.json (separate SHA256 over the operator row JSON and the operator_entities rows JSON, sort_keys=True).
part5_watchtower.note_on_short_prefix_in_task_context: The task brief referenced a short digest prefix '8ec94921...'. Consistent with a prior session's disclosed finding in storage_lifecycle_p5b_r2_1_final_consumer_recensus.json Part 8, this exact prefix does not correspond to any hashing method reconstructable from anything committed in this repo (re-confirmed: grepped for '8ec94921' across the tree, zero matches). This review instead validated against the actual committed, reproducible frozen digests from storage_lifecycle_p5a_part21 (operator_row_sha256=c52d91ce..., operator_entities_rows_sha256=12bd876c...), which are the real canonical freeze values.
part5_watchtower.ordering_pitfall_note: First attempt at this review used 'ORDER BY oe.rowid' for the entity rows and got a DIFFERENT digest (69d9bc20...) than the frozen value. Root-caused before accepting it as a real change: the frozen digest's original methodology relies on the table's natural/entity_address-sorted scan order, not rowid order. Re-ran with 'ORDER BY oe.entity_address' (and separately confirmed with no ORDER BY at all, since SQLite's natural scan order matched) and got an EXACT match to the frozen digest. This was a query-construction artifact on this review's part, not a real WATCHTOWER content change -- disclosed explicitly per the milestone's root-cause-before-accepting-or-rejecting instruction.

terminal_verdict_rationale: This review is being performed roughly 35 minutes after the P5B cutover. Every health, parity, and integrity check performed came back PASS -- writers healthy, new HOT writes proceeding normally, COLD reads healthy via the real production-integrated path, Watchtower and 3SW2 canonical digests byte-identical, CEX/discovery checks all passing, no post-cutover lock incidents, rollback DB frozen and valid. However, the observation-duration gate (Part 14 gate 1) cannot be satisfied this soon after cutover by definition, and independently, HOT->COLD archival automation is confirmed absent (Part 10), which per explicit milestone policy (Part 15) is its own separate reason to retain the rollback DB regardless of the observation clock. Both factors point toward continued retention. The system is healthy; retirement is simply not yet appropriate. Next action: re-run this same review after the full 24-72h observation window has elapsed, and separately begin qualifying (implementing + testing, not activating) the HOT->COLD automation contract in docs/audits/storage_lifecycle_p5c_hot_cold_automation_contract.json as its own follow-on workstream.
